correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge2\) and fixed partition, exact quadratic expansion gives \(\mu=Hx+b+h\operatorname{diag}(H)/2\) and covariance \((\sigma^2/h^2)(I+\sum_a S_aS_a^\top)\). Taking \(\operatorname{tr}(H\operatorname{Cov})\) proves the exact group cost and weighted-cut difference; its covariance trace is always \(2n\sigma^2/h^2\). Graph adjacency Hessians \(I+\epsilon A_G\) are SPD by the spectral norm bound and satisfy \(\kappa_2(H)<1+\delta\) for rational small \(\epsilon\), so standard MAX-CUT reduces exactly. The signed two-dimensional witness yields risks \(3/2\) and \(21/10\). Independently coded exact rational direct enumeration passed 18,107 checks; finite tests do not prove general statements. The unweighted simple MAX-CUT source is Garey–Johnson–Stockmeyer (1976), DOI:10.1016/0304-3975(76)90059-1.

originality.rationale: Brekelmans et al. (2003) already derive the common-basepoint finite-difference cross covariance and the Euclidean norm-error, which are therefore prior ingredients, not new claims. Their fixed-DoE/FFD estimator comparisons do not optimize grouping multiple independent baseline realizations by next-iterate quadratic objective. The 2019 forward-difference source specifies one shared baseline and a norm error criterion. The 2021 interval study optimizes the differencing interval, the 1999 CRN study correlates different simulation-point measurements, and the 2019 interpolation comparison contrasts methods; none of their inspected statements furnishes the exact within-basepoint covariance partition optimum, its signed graph-cut equivalence, Euclidean-risk invariance, or near-isotropic MAX-CUT hardness. Statement-level comparisons, variant/alias queries, primary full-text inspection, and research-index searches completed; residual unindexed priority risk persists.
residual_risks: Unindexed common-random-number allocation, simulation design, and covariance-based finite-difference studies could already contain an equivalent graph-partition theorem.
The full classical generality of finite-difference covariance formulas means the structural identity might be derivable as a corollary of a stronger unsurfaced theorem.
No external independent priority audit has been conducted.
The known single-baseline covariance and Euclidean MSE from Brekelmans et al. must not be interpreted as novel on their own; the claimed advance is the full design/cut equivalence.

value.rationale: A motivated noisy derivative-free estimator faces a natural reference-reuse grouping decision. Its selection is invisible to ordinary Euclidean gradient MSE but exactly controls the next expected quadratic objective through signed Hessian interactions; optimizing the grouping is MAX-CUT hard even for nearly isotropic SPD objectives, and forced separation can reverse the usual belief that less-shared noise must help. This explains a nontrivial computational and statistical tradeoff without asserting general convergence or larger-scale experiments.
